L1724@P42: 58
L1725@P42: The original NEWS scoring system was designed for patients whose normal range for oxygen saturation
L1726@P42: is set at a higher level (ie SpO2 96–100%); for SpO2 values below this, the NEW score increases. Thus, for
L1727@P42: those with hypercapnic respiratory failure and a desired target saturation of 88–92%, the NEWS would
L1728@P42: score 3 points for the low SpO2 and 2 points if supplemental oxygen is required, a total of 5 points. It
L1729@P42: could be argued that this is an appropriate score for a high-risk, acutely ill patient that would prompt
L1730@P42: urgent clinical review. However, after review by a competent clinical decision-maker and confirmation
L1731@P42: that a lower SpO2 range was appropriate, there was no way to reset the scoring system on the NEWS
L1732@P42: chart to demonstrate that, for a patient with hypercapnic respiratory failure, the SpO2 levels are in an
L1733@P42: appropriate range.
L1734@P42: Audits of hospital care have shown that the administration of high-flow oxygen, rather than titrated
L1735@P42: oxygen, to patients with acute exacerbations of COPD increases mortality, hospital length of stay,
L1736@P42: requirement for ventilation, and admission to higher-dependency care.
L1737@P42: 59–62 In contrast, the use of
L1738@P42: titrated oxygen treatment, ie via a Venturi mask, has resulted in less acidosis and reduced mortality. This
L1739@P42: has also been confirmed in the prehospital setting.
L1740@P42: 63
L1741@P42: The NEWS Review Group concluded that the NEWS2 chart could be made safer for patients with
L1742@P42: hypercapnic respiratory failure by having two scoring systems for SpO2:
L1743@P42-43: 20 © Royal College of Physicians 20175 Rationale for updated sections of the NEWS
L1744@P43: 1 the existing SpO2 scoring system (Scale 1) that would apply to the majority of patients
L1745@P43: 2 a dedicated SpO2 scoring system for patients with hypercapnic respiratory failure (Scale 2) whose
L1746@P43: desired oxygen saturations are set at a lower level (88–92%), with the NEWS scoring system
L1747@P43: adjusted accordingly (see below).
L1748@P43: NEWS2 chart oxygen saturation scoring systems: Scale 1 is the usual scale for patients with normal oxygen
L1749@P43: saturation. Scale 2 is the scale to be used for patients with hypercapnic respiratory failure and a
L1750@P43: recommended oxygen saturation range of 88–92%. The section of the chart not being used should be clearly
L1751@P43: crossed out.
L1752@P43: NEWS update: Using the NEWS2 oxygen saturation (SpO2) scoring systems
L1753@P43: • The new SpO2 scoring Scale 2 is for patients with a prescribed oxygen saturation requirement of
L1754@P43: 88–92% (eg in patients with hypercapnic respiratory failure). This should only be used in patients
L1755@P43: confirmed to have hypercapnic respiratory failure on blood gas analysis on either a prior, or their
L1756@P43: current, hospital admission.
L1757@P43: • The decision to use the new SpO2 scoring Scale 2 should be made by a competent clinical decisionmaker and should be recorded in the patient’s clinical notes.
L1758@P43: • In all other circumstances, the regular NEWS SpO2 scoring scale (Scale 1) should be used.
L1759@P43: • For the avoidance of doubt, the SpO2 scoring scale not being used should be clearly crossed out
L1760@P43: across the chart.
L1761@P43: NEWS update: Precise recording of supplemental oxygen delivery
L1762@P43: The mode and rate of oxygen delivery are often poorly documented. Recording the rate of oxygen flow
L1763@P43: (L/min) without recording the mode of delivery or device does not define how much oxygen the patient
L1764@P43: is receiving. The NEWS2 chart has been updated to allow clearer recording of whether the patient is
L1765@P43: breathing air or oxygen; the device being used, if any; and the rate of oxygen delivery. For the
L1766@P43: documentation of the oxygen delivery system, the device codes as recommended by the BTS should be
L1767@P43: used (see Table 1).
L1768@P43: 58
L1769@P43: • We recommend that, when supplemental oxygen is being used to maintain the desired oxygen
L1770@P43: saturation, the rate of oxygen delivery (L/min) and the delivery system/device should be documented
L1771@P43: on the NEWS2 chart using the BTS oxygen delivery system / device codes.
L1772@P43-44: © Royal College of Physicians 2017 21NEWS update: The patient with new confusion or delirium
L1773@P44: Patients with acute illness may develop an acutely altered mental state, manifesting as new confusion,
L1774@P44: delirium or a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) <15. This is an important sign of acute clinical deterioration
L1775@P44: requiring urgent clinical assessment. Acutely altered mentation may occur as a consequence of sepsis,
L1776@P44: hypoxia, hypotension or metabolic disturbances, either alone or in combination.
L1777@P44: The current AVPU scale is designed to record levels of consciousness, but does not record or score newonset confusion or delirium.
L1778@P44: • We recommend including ‘new confusion’ as part of the assessment of consciousness on the NEWS
L1779@P44: chart. The AVPU term has been amended to ACVPU, where C represents new confusion or delirium
L1780@P44: (ie altered mentation).
L1781@P44: • We recommend that new confusion, delirium or acutely altered mentation scores 3 on the NEWS2
L1782@P44: chart, indicating a code red (for a single score of 3), ie that the patient requires urgent assessment.
L1783@P44: • We recommend that if it is unclear whether a patient’s confusion is new or their normal state, the
L1784@P44: confusion should be assumed to be new until confirmed to be otherwise.
